Surah al-Waqi'ah (The Inevitable)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿When the Inevitable Event occurs﴾. It means the Resurrection (qiyamah) has come to pass. It is said: it was described as "the occurring" (al-waqi'ah) because it will certainly happen, as if it were said: "When the event occurs which must inevitably occur." The "occurrence of a matter" (wuqu' al-amr) means its descent (nuzul). It is said: "What I was expecting (atawaqqa'uhu) has occurred," meaning what I was awaiting the descent of (ataraqqabu nuzulahu) has descended. The grammatical position (intisab) of "idha" (when) is due to an implied verb: "remember" (udhkur).

﴿There will be no denying its occurrence.﴾ "A soul that denies" — that is, at the time it occurs there will be no soul that lies about Allah, or denies the unseen, because every soul at that time will be believing, truthful, and affirming. Most souls today are liars and deniers. The lam (ل) here is like its use in His (Exalted) saying: ﴿O, would that I had sent forth [good deeds] for my life!﴾ [al-Fajr: 24].

Verse 3 of Surah al-Waqi'ah (56). Translation:

﴿Abasing [some], exalting [others]﴾. That is: it is abasing and exalting; it raises up peoples and brings others low.

﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾: it is moved with an intense movement, until everything upon it collapses, of mountains and buildings. It is a *badal* (substitution, i.e. apposition in which the second term replaces the first) for "إذا وقعت" (*idha waqaat*, "when it occurs"). It is also permissible for it to be governed by "خافضة رافعة" (*khafidatun rafi'a*, "abasing, exalting"), meaning: it abases and exalts at the time of the shaking of the earth and the crumbling of the mountains.

(p-420) ﴿And the mountains will be crumbled to dust﴾ — and they will be twisted until they become like sawiq (ground grain/flour), or they will be driven, from "bassa al-ghanam" (he drove the sheep), when he drove them, like His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be set in motion﴾ [al-Naba': 20].

﴿So they became scattered dust﴾, dust;

﴿scattered﴾, dispersed.

﴿And you will be [divided into] three kinds (azwājan)﴾, i.e., categories (aṣnāfan). "Azwāj" is said of categories where some are of the same kind as others, or where some of them are mentioned together with others:

﴿three﴿ (thalāthatan): two categories are in Paradise, and one category is in the Fire. Then he explained "azwāj" by saying:

﴿فَأصْحابُ المَيْمَنَةِ﴾: "So the companions of the right hand" (﴿so the companions of the right hand﴾). Here أصحاب (ashab) is the mubtada' (the subject of a nominal sentence, al-mubtada'), and it is unrestricted in its reference. The "they" in the sentence refers to those who are given their records in their right hands.

﴿ما أصْحابُ المَيْمَنَةِ﴾: "What are the companions of the right hand?" Here ما is a mubtada' and أصحاب المَيْمَنَة is its khabar (predicate). This whole sentence is the khabar of the first mubtada' (فأصحاب الميمنة). The phrasing expresses wonder at their state of happiness and magnifies their rank, as if he had said: "What are they?! And what kind of thing are they?!"

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 9:

﴿And the companions of the left hand﴾ — i.e., those who will be given their records in their left hands. Or: "the companions of the lowly station, the wretched and base station," from your saying, "So-and-so is on my right, and so-and-so is on my left," when you describe the two of them as high or low in your esteem. This is because of their being given the right-hand (good) omens and their being given the left-hand (bad) omens. And it has been said: the people of Paradise will be taken to the right, and the people of the Fire to the left.

﴿What are the companions of the left hand?﴾ — i.e., what are they? This is an expression of wonder at their state of wretchedness.

﴿And the foremost﴾: mubtada' (the subject of the nominal sentence), ﴿the foremost﴾: its khabar (the predicate). Its estimated form is: "The foremost to the good things, the foremost to the gardens." It is also said: the second ﴿the foremost﴾ is a ta'kid (emphatic repetition) of the first, and the predicate is:
﴿Those are the ones brought near.﴾ And the first (reading/explanation) is more apt.

In the Gardens of Bliss.

Meaning: they are in the Gardens of Bliss.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 13–14:

﴿A host from among the earlier peoples﴾ ﴿and a few from among the later ones﴾. That is: they are a host (thullah). Al-thullah (a large group of people, a community) refers to a great number of people. The meaning is that the foremost (al-sabiqin) are many from among the earlier peoples, namely the nations from the time of Adam until our Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon them both. "And a few from among the later ones" are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). It has been said: "from among the earlier ones" refers to the earlier ones of this community, and "from among the later ones" refers to its later ones. And it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Both hosts (al-thullatan) together are from my community."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 13–14:

﴿A host from among the earlier peoples﴾ ﴿and a few from among the later ones﴾. That is: they are a host (thullah). Al-thullah (a large group of people, a community) refers to a great number of people. The meaning is that the foremost (al-sabiqin) are many from among the earlier peoples, namely the nations from the time of Adam until our Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon them both. "And a few from among the later ones" are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). It has been said: "from among the earlier ones" refers to the earlier ones of this community, and "from among the later ones" refers to its later ones. And it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Both hosts (al-thullatan) together are from my community."

On thrones (sururin), the plural of "sarir," like "kathib" and "kuthub" (sand dunes),

woven (mawdunatin): interlaced, woven with gold, latticed with pearls and rubies.

Verse 16 is "reclining on them, facing one another" (Qur'an 56:16).

[Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 16:]

﴿Muttaki'in﴾ (reclining) is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in "ʿalā" (upon), and it is the governing element (ʿamil) of that clause, meaning: "They settle upon them, reclining."

﴿ʿAlayha mutaqabilin﴾ (upon them, facing one another): each one looks at the faces of the others, and none of them looks at the backs of the necks of the others. They are described with good companionship, refinement of character, and purity of affection. "Mutaqabilin" is also a circumstantial clause (hal).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 17:

﴿Yatoofu 'alayhim﴾ (circulate among them): yakhdimuhum (serve them).

﴿Wildanun﴾ (youths): ghilmanun (boys), the plural of "walid" (youth).

﴿Mukhalladun﴾ (made to remain): mubqawna abadan ʿala shakli l-wildan (kept forever in the form of youths), lā yatahawwalūna ʿanhu (not changing from it). It was also said: muqarratun (adorned with earrings). Al-khildah (الْخِلْدَةُ) means al-qurt (earring). It was said: they are the children of the people of this world, who had no good deeds for which they would be rewarded, nor bad deeds for which they would be punished. And in a hadith: "The children of the disbelievers are the servants of the people of Paradise."

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 19:**

﴿Neither will they be affected with headache by it﴾ — i.e., because of it. Its literal meaning is: "their headache does not arise from it," or: "they will not be separated from it." "Nor will they be intoxicated" (wa la yunzafun) — and they will not become drunk. "Nuzifa al-rajul" means the man's intellect departed due to intoxication. "Nor will they be intoxicated" (wa la yunzifun), with a kasra on the zay, is the reading of al-Kufiyy (the Kufan reader), meaning: their drink will not run out. It is said: "unzifa al-qawm," when their drink has been exhausted.
[p. 422] ﴿And fruit of what they choose﴾, meaning they take the best and most excellent of it.
﴿And the flesh of birds, of whatever they desire﴾, meaning: whatever they wish for.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 22:

﴿Wa-ḥūrun﴾, the plural of "ḥawrāʾ" (a woman with intense whiteness of the eye and blackness of its iris),

﴿ʿīnun﴾, the plural of "ʿaynāʾ" (a woman with large, beautiful eyes). That is: "And in it are ḥūrun ʿīn," or "And for them are ḥūrun ʿīn." It is also permissible that it be a conjunction with "wildānun" (ḥūrun), "Yazīd, Ḥamzah and ʿAlī" (read it in the genitive, ḥūrin), as a conjunction with "jannāti al-naʿīm" (the gardens of bliss), as if he had said: "They are in gardens of bliss, and fruit, and meat, and ḥūrin."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 23:

﴿Like pearls well-guarded﴾, in clarity and purity,

﴿well-guarded﴾, protected. Al-Zajjaj said: "Like pearls when they come out of their shell, which time has not altered, nor the changing conditions of use."

"As a recompense for what they used to do." ﴿Jaza'an bima kanu ya'malun﴾: "jaza'an" is a maf'ul lahu (object of purpose, i.e. an accusative of reason), meaning that all of that is done to them for the recompense of their deeds; or it is a masdar (verbal noun), meaning they will be recompensed with a recompense.

﴿They will not hear therein﴾, in Paradise,

﴿any vain talk﴾, meaningless speech,

﴿nor any sinful speech﴾, idle chatter.

﴿Illa qīlan salāman salāman﴾: "except the saying: 'Peace, peace.'" It means a saying that is itself a wish of safety (ḥāl of safety). The exception is disjunctive (munqaṭi', i.e., the exception is not from the same category as what precedes it). "Salāman" is either a substitute (badal) for "qīlan," or an object (maf'ūl bihi) of "qīlan," meaning: "They hear in it nothing except that they say: 'Peace, peace.'" The meaning is that they spread the greeting of peace among themselves, so they greet one another with peace after peace.
﴿Among lote-trees without thorns⟩. "Al-sidr" is the jujube tree (shajar al-nabq), and "al-makhdud" is that which has no thorns, as if its thorns had been cut away.
﴿And acacia trees arranged in layers﴾. "Al-talh" is the banana tree, and "al-mandud" is that which is arranged with fruit from its base to its top, so that no bare stalk shows.
﴿And shade extended﴾, stretched out and spread wide, like the shade between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun.
(p-423) ﴿And flowing water﴾: running, without limit or ditch; that is, it flows over the ground without a trench.
﴿And fruit in abundance﴾, i.e., abundant in kinds.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 33:

﴿Neither cut off﴾, meaning not cut off at certain times, like the fruits of this world; rather, they are everlasting,

﴿nor forbidden﴾, meaning not withheld from the one who reaches for them in any way. It is also said: "not cut off" by time, and "not forbidden" by price.

And upon raised couches (furush marfu'a)—elevated in rank, or piled up until they are raised high, or raised upon the beds. It was also said: they are the women, because a woman is referred to by the word "bed" (firash). Raised upon the arā'ik (couches), as Allah (Exalted) says: ﴿They and their spouses are in shade, reclining upon couches﴾ [Ya-Sin: 56]. And His saying indicates this:

Verse 56:35: ﴿Indeed, We have created them with a special creation﴾. He [Allah] initiated their creation as a fresh beginning, without birth. So the intended referent may be either those whose creation was newly initiated, or those whose creation was renewed. On any interpretation other than this one, [the women] are left implicit (uḍmira lahunna), because the mention of the furush (the couches, i.e. the reclining places) indicates them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 36:

﴿We have made them virgins﴾, (i.e.) maidens; whenever their husbands come to them, they find them virgins.

﴿عُرُبًا﴾ ["ʿuruban"], read by Ḥamzah, Khalaf, Yaḥyā and Ḥammād, is the plural of ﴿عَرُوبٌ﴾ ["ʿarūb"], meaning a woman who is affectionate and endearing to her husband, and good in her *tabaʿʿul* (conduct toward her husband, i.e., her good behaviour and devotion as a wife).

﴿أتْرابًا﴾ ["atrāban"] means of equal age, the daughters of thirty-three years, and their husbands are likewise, and the lām in
﴿For the companions of the right﴾, it is connected to "We created them" (anshanā).

ثُلَّةٌ: that is, the companions of the right hand are a multitude (ثُلَّةٌ),

﴿مِنَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ "from the earlier generations" ﴿وَثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الآخِرِينَ﴾ "and a multitude from the later generations." If it is asked: how did He say before this, "and few from the later generations," and then say here, "and a multitude from the later generations"? I say: that (statement) concerns the foremost (al-sabiqun), and this concerns the companions of the right hand, and that they are numerous from the earlier and the later generations alike. And from al-Hasan: "The foremost of the (previous) nations are more numerous than the foremost of our nation, and the followers of the (previous) nations are like the followers of this nation."

ثُلَّةٌ: that is, the companions of the right hand are a multitude (ثُلَّةٌ),

﴿مِنَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ "from the earlier generations" ﴿وَثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الآخِرِينَ﴾ "and a multitude from the later generations." If it is asked: how did He say before this, "and few from the later generations," and then say here, "and a multitude from the later generations"? I say: that (statement) concerns the foremost (al-sabiqun), and this concerns the companions of the right hand, and that they are numerous from the earlier and the later generations alike. And from al-Hasan: "The foremost of the (previous) nations are more numerous than the foremost of our nation, and the followers of the (previous) nations are like the followers of this nation."

Translation:

﴿And the companions of the left hand — what are the companions of the left hand?﴾ "Al-shimal" (the left) and "al-mash'amah" (the left side) are one and the same.

(p-424) ﴿In scorching wind﴾, in a heat of fire that penetrates the pores,

﴿and boiling water﴾, and hot water, extremely intense in its heat.
﴿And a shade of black smoke﴾, from a smoke that is intensely black.

Not cool nor generous.

This is a negation of the two qualities of shade from it. He means that it is a shade, but not like other shades. He called it "shade," then negated from it the coolness of shade and its refreshment and benefit for the one who takes refuge in it from the harm of heat, and that is its generosity, so as to erase what the meaning of "shade" implies of finding relief in it. The meaning is that it is a shade that is hot and harmful.

Indeed they were, before that, ﴿mutrafin﴾ (those given to luxury), i.e., in the world, ﴿mutrafin﴾, made comfortable and pampered, so that this prevented them from being restrained and occupied them away from taking warning.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 46:**

﴿And they used to persist﴾, i.e., they kept on (yuduwamuna),

﴿in the great violation﴾. That is: in the great sin, or in shirk, because it is the breaking of the covenant of the pact. And "al-hinth" (violation): the breaking of a covenant reinforced by an oath, or disbelief in the Resurrection, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die﴾ [al-Nahl: 38].

﴿They used to say: "When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be raised up again?"﴾ Its estimated form is: "Will we be raised up when we die?" The verb "we are raised up" (*yub'athu*, أنُبْعَثُ) is the governing element (*'amil*) of the adverbial of time (*zarf*), and it is permissible to omit it, since "مَبْعُوثُونَ" (*mab'uthun*, "raised up") indicates it. However, "مَبْعُوثُونَ" does not govern the adverbial, because "إنَّ" (*inna*, "indeed") and the interrogative particle (*al-istifham*) prevent what follows them from governing what precedes them.

ﷺ-free passage; translating faithfully.

﴿Or [will] our forefathers, the former ones?﴾ The interrogative hamza has entered upon the conjunctive particle (ḥarf al-ʿaṭf), and the conjunction upon the pronoun in "lamabʿūthūn" (we shall indeed be resurrected) is permissible without emphasis by "naḥnu" (we), because of the intervening element, which is the hamza, just as it is permissible in His saying: ﴿Neither we nor our forefathers would have associated [anything with Him]﴾ [al-Anʿām: 148], owing to the separating "lā" (not), which emphasizes the negation. "Or our forefathers" is the reading of Madani and Shami [readers].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verses 49–50:

﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter﴾ ﴿will surely be gathered together to the appointed time of a known day﴾, to the day that the world has been appointed for, a known day. The genitive construction here carries the meaning of "min" (of/from), as in "a ring of silver" (khatam fiddah). Al-mi'qat (the appointed time) is that by which a thing is timed, i.e., limited; from it come "mawaqit al-ihram" (the fixed places of ihram), which are the boundaries that whoever wishes to enter Makkah may not cross except in the state of ihram.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verses 49–50:

﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter﴾ ﴿will surely be gathered together to the appointed time of a known day﴾, to the day that the world has been appointed for, a known day. The genitive construction here carries the meaning of "min" (of/from), as in "a ring of silver" (khatam fiddah). Then indeed you, O you who go astray (from guidance),

the deniers (of the Resurrection), and they are the people of Makkah and those in a similar condition to theirs.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 52:

﴿Indeed, you will be eating from a tree﴾. "Min" (from) here indicates the starting point (ibtida' al-ghayah, the origin or source).

﴿from zaqqum﴾. "Min" here explains (bayan) the tree, specifying what kind of tree it is.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verses 53–54:

﴿Then you will fill your bellies from it﴾ ﴿and drink on top of it from the boiling water﴾. He made the pronoun referring to the tree feminine according to its meaning, and masculine according to its wording, in "minha" (from it) and "alayhi" (on it).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verses 53–54:

﴿Then you will fill your bellies from it﴾ ﴿and drink on top of it from the boiling water﴾. He made the pronoun referring to the tree feminine according to its meaning, and masculine according to its wording, in "minha" (from it) and "alayhi" (on it).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 55:

﴿Fa-shāribūna shurba﴾, with the shīn vowelled with a ḍamma (shurb), is the reading of Madanī, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and Sahl; the others read it with a fatḥa (sharb). Both are verbal nouns (maṣdar).

﴿al-Hīm﴾ are camels that are thirsty and never quench their thirst; it is the plural of ahyam and haymā᾽ (masc. and fem. of the adjective meaning "thirsty"). The meaning is that there is inflicted upon them, from hunger, what compels them to eat the zaqqūm, which is like molten metal (al-muhl). When they fill their bellies with it, there is inflicted upon them, from thirst, what compels them to drink the ḥamīm (boiling water), which cuts their intestines to pieces; so they drink it as thirsty camels drink water. The coordination of "those who drink" (al-shāribūna) upon "those who drink" (al-shāribūna) is valid, although the two refer to the same persons and are two identical descriptions, because their being drinkers of the ḥamīm in the state of its extreme heat and the cutting of their intestines is a wondrous matter, and their drinking it in that state, as thirsty camels drink water, is also a wondrous matter. Thus the two are two different descriptions.

﴿This is their hospitality﴾, which is the provision prepared for the guest as an honour to him,

﴿on the Day of Judgment﴾, the Day of Recompense.

Quran 56:57: "We created you, so why do you not affirm (the truth)?"

Here "fa-lawlā" means "fa-hallā" ("why not" / "then why not"). The verb "tuṣaddiqūn" is a ḥaḍḍ (exhortation, a urging to act): it urges them to affirm.

This affirmation may be of the creation: although they do affirm it, their doctrine opposes what affirmation requires, so they are as though they were deniers of it. Or it may be of the resurrection (al-ba'th), because the one who created at first is not precluded from creating a second time.

Translation:

﴿Have you considered that which you emit?﴾ That is, that which you emit (tumnūnahu), i.e., that which you eject into the wombs, of the seminal drops (min al-nutaf).
(p. 426) ﴿Is it you who create it?﴾ That is, you determine it, shape it, and make it a complete human being. ﴿Or are We the Creators?﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 60:

﴿We have decreed death among you﴾, [that is] a decreeing, and We have distributed it among you as the distribution of provisions, with variation and difference, as Our will requires. So your lifespans differ: short, long, and intermediate. "Qadarna" (قَدَرْنا), with the light pronunciation (bi-l-takhfif), is [the reading] of Ibn Kathir (Makki). "Sabaqtuhu bi-l-shay'" (سَبَقْتُهُ بِالشَيْءِ) means: when I render him unable to attain it and overcome him in it. So the meaning of His saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 61:

﴿And We are not to be outdone﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 60] ﴿in replacing your likenesses﴾: We are capable of that, and you cannot overpower Us in it. "Amthalakum" is the plural of "mithl" (likeness), meaning: in replacing from among you, and in your place, others like you from among creation.

﴿And to bring you into being in what you do not know﴾: and to bring you into being in a form of creation that you do not know and have not experienced the like of. That is, We are capable of both matters together: creating what resembles you and what does not resemble you. So how could We be unable to restore you?

It is also permissible that "amthalakum" is the plural of "mathal" (attribute, description), meaning: in order to change and alter your attributes that you have in your creation and your characters, and to bring you into being in attributes that you do not know.

﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾. The word "al-nashā'ata" (اَلنَّشاءَةَ) is read this way by Makki and Abu 'Amr.

﴿So why do you not remember?﴾ This means that whoever has power over a thing once is not prevented from having power over it a second time. In this is evidence for the validity of qiyas (analogy), since He reproached them for failing to draw the analogy of the later creation from the first.

Surah 56, verse 63:

﴿Have you considered what you plant?﴾ What you sow of food, i.e., you till the land and cast into it the seed.

﴿Do you cause it to grow, or do We cause it to grow?﴾ That is: do you make it sprout and bring it forth as a plant?

﴿Or are We the sowers?﴾ That is, the ones who cause it to grow.

In a hadith it is said: "None of you should say, 'I have sown (zara'tu),' but let him say, 'I have ploughed (haratu).'"

(p-427) ﴿If We willed, We would have made it into debris (ḥuṭāman)﴾: dry, crumbled stalks (hashīman), broken into pieces (mutakassiran), before it ripened (qabla idrākihi).

﴿Then you would have been left wondering (tafakkahūn)﴾: you would be astonished (taʿjabūn), or you would regret (tandamūn) your toil in it and your expenditure upon it, or regret the sins you had committed, on account of which you were struck with this.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 66:

﴿إنّا﴾ meaning: you say, "Innā" (إنّا), "a-innā" (أإنا), "Abū Bakr" (أبُو بَكْرٍ),

﴿لَمُغْرَمُونَ﴾ (“Indeed, we are burdened with debt”): that is, we are burdened with the cost of what we have spent, or we are destroyed by the loss of our provision, from "al-gharam" (الْغَرامُ), which is destruction.

"Rather, we are" — a people,

"deprived" — (meaning) impoverished, cut off from provision (muharafun), (meaning) ill-starred (mahdudun), not fortunate (la majdudun); we have no share (la hazza lana), and no good fortune (la bakht lana); and had we been fortunate (majdudin), this would not have befallen us.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 68:

﴿Have you then considered the water which you drink?﴾ That is: the sweet water, fit for drinking.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 69:

﴿Have you brought it down from the muzn, that is, the white cloud, and it is the sweetest of water,

or are We the ones who send it down?﴾ by Our power.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 56, verse 70:

﴿If We willed, We would make it unfit (ujaj)﴾, meaning salty or bitter, so that it could not be drunk.

﴿Why then do you not give thanks?﴾ That is, "fa-halla tashkurun?" (Why do you not give thanks?). The lam (اللام) entered upon the response of *law* (لَوْ, "if") in His words, ﴿We would surely make it crumbled debris﴾ (لَجَعَلْناهُ حُطامًا), but it was removed here. This is because *law*, when it governs two clauses whose second clause is linked to the first in the way a response (jaza') is linked to a condition (shart), and when it is not purely conditional like *in* (إنْ, "if") and does not operate in the same way, has the sense of a condition by implication. It indicates that the second clause was negated because the first was negated. Therefore it requires, in its response, something that marks this linkage, so this lam was added to serve as a marker of that. Since its position was well known, its removal from the wording was not a concern, because everyone knows it, and the two states of omitting it and including it are equal. Moreover, its earlier mention, given that the distance between them is short, makes it unnecessary to mention it again.

Also, this lam necessarily conveys the sense of emphasis (ta'kid). It was therefore included in the verse about food, and not in the verse about drink, to indicate that the matter of food takes precedence over the matter of drink, and that the warning of its loss is more severe and harder to bear. This is because drink is needed only as a complement to food. For this reason the verse about food was placed before the verse about drink.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 71:

(p-428) ﴿Have you then considered the fire which you kindle?﴾ That is, you strike it and extract it from the firestarters (al-zind). The Arabs strike fire with two pieces of wood, rubbing one against the other. They call the upper one "al-zand" and the lower one "al-zanda." They likened them to the stallion (al-fahl) and the mare (al-taruqa).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 72:

﴿Do you bring it into being, or are We the Producers?﴾ That is, the tree from which the firestarter (al-zinad) comes.

﴿Or are We the Producers?﴾ That is, the Creators of it at its beginning, without precedent.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 73:**

﴿We have made it﴾, namely the Fire,

﴿a reminder﴾, a reminder of the Fire of Jahannam, in that We have attached to it the means of livelihood, and We have made the need for it a trial common to all, so that it is ever present before people; they look at it and remember what they have been threatened with.

﴿and a provision﴾, and a benefit,

﴿for the wayfarers﴾, for the travellers who stop in the *qawa'* (the desert wastes), or for those whose stomachs or provision-bags of food have become empty. It comes from their saying "*aqwat al-dar*" (the house became empty), when it has been emptied of its inhabitants. He began with mention of the creation of man, saying: ﴿Have you considered the semen you emit?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 58], because the blessing in it precedes all other blessings; then with that by which its sustenance is maintained, which is the grain, so He said: ﴿Have you considered the seed you sow?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 63]; then with that by which one kneads and with which one drinks, which is water; then with that by which one bakes, which is fire. Thus the obtaining of food is by the combination of these three, and the body cannot do without it as long as it is alive.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 74:

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord﴾, i.e., declare your Lord free of whatever is unfitting for Him, O listener, O one who reflects. Or by "the name" he meant the remembrance (dhikr), i.e., "glorify by remembering your Lord,"

﴿the Mighty﴾: an adjective of the first noun (al-mudaf), or of the second (al-mudaf ilayhi). It was also said: "Say, Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty." And it was narrated in a marfu' report that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Make it in your bowing (ruku')."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 75:

﴿Fa-lā uqsimu﴾ — that is, "fa-uqsimu" (so I swear). The "lā" is extra (zā'idah), serving to emphasize (mu'akkidah), like its use in His saying: ﴿so that the People of the Scripture may know﴾ [al-Hadid: 29]. It is also read "fa-la-uqsimu," meaning "fa-la-anā uqsimu" (so truly I swear). The lām here is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtida'), which entered upon a nominal sentence consisting of a subject and predicate, namely "anā uqsimu" (I swear), and then the subject was omitted. The lām cannot be the lām of oath (lām al-qasam), because its proper accompaniment is the emphatic nūn (al-nūn al-mu'akkidah).

﴿bi-mawāqi' al-nujūm﴾ — by their setting-places (bi-masāqitihā), and their places of setting (magharibihā). It is read "bi-mawqi'" by Hamzah and ʿAlī (p-429). Perhaps God (Exalted is He), at the end of the night, when the stars sink toward the west, has specific great acts (af'āl makhṣūṣah ʿaẓīmah), or for the angels there are described acts of worship ('ibādāt mawṣūfah), or because it is the time when those who pray at night (al-mutahajjidīn) stand, and mercy and good pleasure descend upon them. Therefore He swore by their places, and magnified that by His saying:

﴿And indeed, it is an oath, if you knew, a great one﴾. It is an interposition (i'tirad) within an interposition, because it was inserted between the oath and that which the oath is about, which is His saying:

Verse 77: ﴿Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an﴾. (It is) good, pleasing; or beneficial, abounding in benefits; or noble with Allah. And "if you only knew" is interposed between the described (noun) and its description.

In a Book well-guarded (kitab maknun) — that is, the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz),

﴿in a Book well-guarded﴾ — protected from falsehood reaching it, or from anyone other than the angels who are brought near (al-muqarrabun). None other than them can gain access to it.

Qur'an 56:79: ﴿None touches it except the purified.﴾ (They are) purified from all impurities, the impurities of sins and others, if you make the clause a description of "a Book well-guarded," which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh). If you make it a description of the Qur'an, then the meaning is: it is not fitting that it be touched except by one who is in a state of purity (ṭahārah) among people, and what is meant is touching what is written in it.

﴿A revelation﴾: a fourth attribute (ṣifah, a descriptive qualifier) of the Qur'an, meaning *munazzal* (sent down).

﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾. Or it is a description by means of the verbal noun (maṣdar), because it was sent down in stages, distinct from the rest of God's books. So it is, in itself, a *tanzil*. For this reason it took the place of some of its names, and it is said: "It has come in the *Tanzil* that such-and-such," and "the *Tanzil* has spoken of it." Or [the phrase may be read as] "it is a *tanzil*," with the subject (mubtada', the subject of a nominal sentence) omitted.

﴿Is it this discourse﴾, that is, the Qur'an,

﴿that you are ones who disregard it﴾ (mudhinun), treating it lightly, like one who is lax (yudhinu) in some matter, that is, he softens his side and does not stand firm in it, out of negligence toward it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 82:

﴿And you make your provision [consist in] that you deny﴾. That is: you make the thanks for your provision to be denial; that is, you put denial in the place of thanks. In the reading of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), which is (p-430) the reading of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "And you make your thanks [consist in] that you deny," that is: you make your thanks for the blessing of the Qur'an to be that you deny it. It was also said: it was revealed concerning the anwāʾ (the rising and setting of stars, by which the Arabs attributed rain to stars), and their attribution of the rain (al-suqyā) to them. And "al-rizq" (provision) here means the rain; that is: you make the thanks for what Allah provides you of rain to be that you deny that it comes from Allah, in that you attribute it to the stars.

﴿Then why, when it reaches the throat﴾, [i.e., "the soul" (al-nafs)], that is, "the spirit" (al-rooh), at the time of death,

﴿the throat﴾, the passage of food and drink.

And you at that time are looking on.

The address is to those present with the dying person at that hour.

[Surah al-Waqi'ah, 56:85] "And We are nearer to him than you are, but you do not see."

Al-Nasafi's commentary: "And We are nearer to him" — to the one dying (al-muhtadar). "Than you are" — "but you do not see" — you do not understand (la ta'qilun), and you do not know (la ta'lamun).
﴿Then why not, if you are not to be held accountable﴾, that is, not subject to a lord, from "dāna al-sultān al-ra'iyyah" (the ruler governed his subjects), when he managed them.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 87:**

﴿تَرْجِعُونَها﴾ — "you return it": you return the *nafs* (soul), which is the *ruh* (spirit), to the body, after it has reached the *hulqum* (the throat).

﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ — "if you are truthful": that you are not subject to lordship, not overpowered. In the two verses, *law-la* (هَلَّا / لَوْلَا, "why not" / "if only"), is for *tahdid* (urging, reproach), and it calls for a verb, which is "tarji'unaha" ("you return it"). He suffices with mentioning it once. The arrangement of the verse is: "So why, when it reaches the throat, do you not return it, if you are not subject to debt?" The second *fa-law-la* is repeated for emphasis. "And We are nearer to him than you" — O people of the dead person — by Our power and Our knowledge, or by the angels of death.

The meaning is: you, in your denial of the signs of God in everything, if He sends down to you a miraculous Book, you say: "It is magic and fabrication"; and if He sends to you a truthful messenger, you say: "He is a sorcerer, a liar"; and if He gives you rain by which He gives you life, you say: "It is the star of such-and-such." This is according to a doctrine that leads to neglect and nullification. So why do you not return the spirit to the body after it has reached the throat, if there is no one who takes it, and you are truthful in your nullification and your disbelief in the One who gives life and causes death, who originates and restores?

"Then if he was one of those brought near" — the one who has died, if he was among the foremost (al-muqarrabin), among the three kinds of spouses mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

Wait, the passage is short; I should translate faithfully, keeping the structure. The first-time technical term gloss: "al-muqarrabin" isn't really a technical term requiring transliteration glossing, but tafsir-like terms... Keep it simple.

**Translation:**

﴿Then if he was﴾, the one who has died,

﴿of those brought near﴾, that is, of the foremost (al-sabiqun) among the three groups of spouses mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

"Then rest" (fa-rawh): then he has repose (istirahah).

"And provision" (rayhan): and sustenance (rizq).

"And a Garden of Delight."

(p-431) ﴿Then, "Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand."﴾ That is: "Peace be upon you, O companion of the right hand, from your brethren, the companions of the right hand"; that is, they greet you with peace. This is like His saying: ﴿except the saying "Peace, peace."﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 26]

And as for the one who is of the deniers, the astray (wa-amma in kana min al-mukadhdhibin al-dallin), they are the third category of the three kinds of spouses (azwaj), and they are those to whom it was said in this surah: ﴿Then indeed you, O astray deniers,﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 51]

﴿فَنُـزُلٌ مِن حَمِيمٍ﴾ ﴿وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ﴾ "But for him is a welcome of scalding water, and burning in the Blazing Fire." Ay: idkhalun fihi ("it means entering into it").

In these verses there is an indication that all disbelief (kufr) is one religion (millah wahidah), and that the people of major sins (ashab al-kaba'ir) are among the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin), because they are not deniers (mukadhdhibin).

﴿فَنُـزُلٌ مِن حَمِيمٍ﴾ ﴿وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ﴾ "But for him is a welcome of scalding water, and burning in the Blazing Fire." Ay: idkhalun fihi ("it means entering into it").

In these verses there is an indication that all disbelief (kufr) is one religion (millah wahidah), and that the people of major sins (ashab al-kaba'ir) are among the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin), because they are not deniers (mukadhdhibin).

Indeed, this (ﷺ-free) — "this" refers to what was sent down in this surah,

﴿Indeed, this is the certain truth of certainty﴾ — that is, the established truth of certainty (ḥaqq al-yaqīn).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 56, verse 96:

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty.﴾

It is narrated that ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (may Allah be pleased with him) entered upon Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him) during his final illness, and he said to him: "What do you complain of?" He said: "My sins." He said: "What do you desire?" He said: "The mercy of my Lord." He said: "Shall we not call a physician?" He said: "The physician has made me ill." He said: "Shall we not order your gift (ʿaṭāʾ) to be given?" He said: "I have no need of it." He said: "We will hand it over to your daughters." He said: "They have no need of it. I have instructed them to recite Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever recites Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah every night will never suffer poverty.'"

And there is no mention of "Allah" in these three surahs: "Iqtarabat" (al-Qamar), "al-Raḥmān," and "al-Wāqiʿah."
